message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: dotnet

on:
  push:
    branches: [ master ]
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
      - "docs/**"
  pull_request:
    branches: [ master ]
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
      - "docs/**"

concurrency:
  group: dotnet-${{ github.ref }}-1
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm, macos-latest ]

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    - name: Setup .NET
      uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
      with:
        dotnet-version: |
          11.0.x
    - name: Cache NuGet packages
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.nuget/packages
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-${{ hashFiles('**/*.csproj', '**/packages.lock.json') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-
    - name: Restore dependencies
      run: dotnet restore
    - name: Build
      run: dotnet build --no-restore -c Release
    - name: Test
      run: dotnet test -c Release --no-build",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs dotnet restore on every matrix job without caching NuGet packages, so repeated dependency fetching occurs across runs. Pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (Cache dependency downloads) fits: preconditions hold because dependency fetching is repeated and measurable, and cache inputs can include the lockfile/project files plus runner OS. Contraindications do not apply: NuGet packages are immutable/content-addressed, and no equivalent cache exists in the workflow. The change adds a cache step before dotnet restore while keeping restore, build, and test steps intact, preserving all required checks and coverage. Stale-run cancellation is already present via the existing concurrency block, and fail-fast is already the GitHub Actions default for the matrix, so no other pattern adds value here.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
